govdocs-archive_org-nMonroeByCapellFranc: Frank A. Capell’s Strange Death of Marilyn Monroe — this archive.org file — questions the official account of her death. The 1964 pamphlet belongs to alternative true-crime literature. Its theories remain disputed. The case still fascinates. The book should be read critically.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIAEuropeSecret: Clare Pedrick’s piece — CIA Organized Secret Army in Western Europe — covers the stay-behind networks. Gladio was the Italian arm. The networks stayed secret for decades. The file belongs to the intelligence archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIAPressSelf-Pr: Bill Richards’s piece — First It Was ‘The FBI’ on TV, and Next It May Be the CIA — covers the agency’s PR push. The agency courted Hollywood. The file belongs to the intelligence archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FrankShirleyRos: This FBI memorandum on Shirley Rose Frank — September 30, 1964 — is a Bureau file. The declassified memo is a primary source. The Bureau tracked countless citizens. The memo may hold a clue. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the government archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-JacksonJesse_Ja: John Pekkanen’s The Jesse Jackson Style: Militant but Nonviolent profiles the leader. Jackson rose from the civil rights movement. The profile is sharp. His style was unique. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-JamesRosemaryWa: This FBI memorandum on the attempt to involve Walter Jenkins — March — is a Bureau file. The declassified memo is a primary source. Jenkins was LBJ’s top aide. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the political archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ODanielWLeeSena: This item — ODaniel, W. Lee: Senator — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
the-story-of-a-white-rocking-horse: Laura Lee Hope, creator of the beloved Bobbsey Twins, wrote this gentle tale for very young readers. At its center is a handsome white rocking horse — a treasured toy whose adventures delight the children who love him. Told in simple language with a warm, old-fashioned charm, the story suits bedtime reading and early readers just finding their way with books.
seven-maids-of-far-cathay-being-english-: Mary Forman Ledyard taught in China and wrote these sketches from what she saw in her own classroom. Each chapter introduces a Chinese schoolgirl — her family, her lessons, her hopes — giving English readers a personal look at girlhood in early-twentieth-century China. The book is gentle and observant, valuing its young subjects as individuals rather than curiosities.
the-little-lady-of-the-big-house: Jack London's final novel unfolds on a great California ranch, where Dick Forrest has built an agricultural empire — and where his spirited wife Paula falls in love with his old friend Evan Graham. The triangle plays out among horses, harvests, and wide skies. Part romance, part hymn to the farming life London himself loved, it was the last book he finished.
poems-of-purpose: Ella Wheeler Wilcox — famous for Laugh, and the world laughs with you — gathers her most uplifting verse in this collection. Her poems urge courage, kindness, and perseverance in plain, musical language that millions loved. Though critics sniffed, ordinary readers took her words to heart, making her one of America's most quoted poets.
the-old-stone-house: Constance Fenimore Woolson — friend of Henry James and a fine novelist in her own right — sets this story in an old stone house heavy with memory. Her characters confront the past's hold on the present with quiet intensity. Woolson's subtle, observant fiction rewards readers who appreciate craft and psychological depth.
the-hero-of-hill-house: Mabel Hale's school story crowns its hero of Hill House — a boy whose pluck and honor win the day. Games, lessons, and tests of character fill these wholesome pages. A fine, clean tale for young readers. Through games bravely played and temptations resisted, he proves what a true Hill House boy should be.
good-sense: Baron d'Holbach's Good Sense — the bible of French atheism — argues for reason against religion in plain, forceful prose. Its calm radicalism shocked the 18th century. A classic of Enlightenment thought. Priests and kings found it dangerous; philosophers found it liberating.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-and-sch: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey and School of Clonmacnoise — St. Ciaran's great Irish monastery on the Shannon — celebrates its golden age of learning. John Healy writes with patriotic warmth. A treasured reference on Ireland's monastic glory. High crosses still stand where the scholars once walked.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-melr: A 1913 entry on Melrose, the border abbey of Scotland. Bruce's heart lies in its choir. Michael Barrett recounts its ruined glory. Scott's moonlight made it famous. The heart of the Bruce was buried before its high altar. Its east window is the pride of the Borders.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-newh: The Encyclopedia on Newhouse, England's first Premonstratensian house. Lincolnshire's fens heard the white canons' chant. Francis Martin Geudens gives its story. A pioneer house of a new order. The order's English story starts at its Lincolnshire gate. Its canons wore white over black.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alessandro-fa: This 1913 reference article on Alessandro Farnese — the cardinal, grandson of Paul III. Umberto Benigni traces his splendid career. His palace and villa dazzled Rome. The Church's grandest patron of art. A prince of the Renaissance curia. His patronage built the Gesu church.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-of-repo: This 1913 reference article on the altar of repose — the Holy Thursday repository. Andrew Meehan describes its veiled glory. The Host rests there till Good Friday. The faithful watch through the night. Gethsemane's yearly memorial. Its flowers veil the hidden God.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-vase: A 1913 entry on altar vases — the vessels for the altar's flowers. Augustin Schulte notes their decent use. Lilies and roses grace the feast. Their blooms honor the sacrifice. The altar's floral servants. Their water keeps the blossoms fresh. Their pairs flank the crucifix.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-see-o: This 1913 reference piece on the ancient see of Odense — the bishopric of St. Canute's isle. Arthur Taylor tells its story. The martyr king fell in its church. The Reformation closed the old see. A vanished bishopric of Fyn. Its Canute shrine drew the pilgrims.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anise: This 1913 reference article on anise — the biblical herb of the tithe. Edward Arbez notes its scriptural mention. The Pharisees tithed its tiny seeds. Christ rebuked their trifling care. A small herb of the Gospel. Its seeds flavor the Christmas cakes.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apocalypse: A 1913 entry on the Apocalypse — St. John's book of the last things. Christian Van den Biesen unfolds its visions. The Lamb conquers the beast. The Church reads it in hope. Scripture's most mysterious book. Its letters warn the seven churches.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-appeal-as-fro: This 1913 reference piece on the appel comme d'abus — the French appeal against church abuse. Richard Burtsell explains its Gallican use. The state checked the Church's courts. The Revolution swept it away. A weapon of the old regime. Its use vexed the Gallican bishops.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apse: This 1913 reference article on the apse — the semicircular sanctuary. Thomas Poole traces its Roman roots. The bishop's throne stood in its curve. The basilicas kept the ancient form. The church's sacred head. Its vault glows with mosaic gold. Its conch holds the enthroned Christ.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-archdiocese: This 1913 reference piece on the archdiocese — the chief see of its province — sets out its place. The archbishop rules his own flock. The nearby bishops look to his chair. His church is the province's crown. The mother see of the region.
